sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In San Francisco, the area south of Market Street is called Soma.
sentences.zh: 在旧金山，市场街以南的地区被称为索玛。

sentences.en: The part of town north of the Panhandle is known as NOPA.
sentences.zh: 狭长地带以北的那片城区被称为诺帕。

sentences.en: Just north of our office is a part of town that Oakland is trying to brand as Kono,
sentences.zh: 就在我们办公室北边，有一片城区奥克兰正试图将其包装为科诺，

sentences.en: short for Koreatown Northgate, but no one actually calls it that.
sentences.zh: 也就是韩国城北门区的简称，但其实没人这么叫它。

sentences.en: I live in a part of town at the intersection of North Oakland, Berkeley, and Emeryville.
sentences.zh: 我住在北奥克兰、伯克利和埃默里维尔交界处的一个片区。

sentences.en: A neighborhood real estate brokers are calling NOB.
sentences.zh: 一个房地产经纪人称之为诺布的街区。

sentences.en: That's producer Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人艾弗里·特鲁弗莱曼。

sentences.en: The whole NOB thing makes me feel pretty icky.
sentences.zh: 整个诺布这个说法让我觉得挺恶心的。

sentences.en: These abbreviated neighborhood names are such cliches.
sentences.zh: 这些缩写的街区名字简直就是陈词滥调。

sentences.en: Like there's that episode of South Park where part of town gets rebranded as
sentences.zh: 就像《南方公园》里有一集，那片城区被重新包装成

sentences.en: South of Downtown South Park or Sodo Sopa.
sentences.zh: 市中心南方公园或索多索帕。

sentences.en: There's a certain quality to the vibe and energy that is Sodo Sopa.
sentences.zh: 索多索帕那种氛围和活力有一种特质。

sentences.en: From the independent merchants and unique cafes to the rustic charm of a mixed income crowd.
sentences.zh: 从独立商户和独特咖啡馆，到各种收入人群混杂的乡村魅力。

sentences.en: In an episode of How I Met Your Mother, two characters buy an apartment in Doe Wee Satripla.
sentences.zh: 在《老爸老妈浪漫史》的一集里，两个角色在多维萨特里普拉买了一套公寓。

sentences.en: Doe Wee Satripla.
sentences.zh: 多维萨特里普拉。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: You're not New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 你们俩不是纽约人。

sentences.en: Oh, no, actually, we live on the Upper West Side.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，其实我们住在上西区。

sentences.en: No need to be embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 不用觉得不好意思。

sentences.en: Listen, here in New York, we just shorten the names of all the neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 听着，在纽约，我们只是把所有街区名字都缩写了。

sentences.en: Soho, Tribeca, Nolita.
sentences.zh: 苏荷、翠贝卡、诺利塔。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Doe Wee Satripla.
sentences.zh: 多维萨特里普拉。

sentences.en: No, I'm from New York.
sentences.zh: 不，我是纽约人。

sentences.en: I know this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我知道这个街区。

sentences.en: Doe Wee Satripla turns out to be short for Downwind of the Sewage Treatment Plant.
sentences.zh: 原来多维萨特里普拉是污水处理厂下风向的简称。

sentences.en: There are brokers who are renaming parts of Harlem as Soha, parts of Little Italy as Nolita,
sentences.zh: 有些经纪人把哈莱姆区的部分地区重新命名为索哈，把小意大利的部分地区命名为诺利塔，

sentences.en: marketing the Bronx as Sobro.
sentences.zh: 把布朗克斯推销为索布罗。

sentences.en: This is Congressman Hakeem Jeffries.
sentences.zh: 这是国会议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯。

sentences.en: He represents New York's 8th Congressional District, which is Brooklyn and parts of Queens.
sentences.zh: 他代表纽约州第八国会选区，即布鲁克林和皇后区的一部分。

sentences.en: These are names that are created out of thin air.
sentences.zh: 这些名字都是凭空捏造出来的。

sentences.en: They're fantasy.
sentences.zh: 它们是幻想。

sentences.en: They're fiction.
sentences.zh: 它们是虚构。

sentences.en: They're made up solely, in my view, to artificially inflate prices.
sentences.zh: 依我看，它们纯粹是为了人为抬高价格而编造的。

sentences.en: Before Congressman Jeffries was elected to the House of Representatives,
sentences.zh: 在杰弗里斯议员当选众议员之前，

sentences.en: he was a member of the New York State Legislature,
sentences.zh: 他是纽约州议会的成员，

sentences.en: and he saw these neighborhood abbreviations creep into his jurisdiction.
sentences.zh: 他眼看着这些街区缩写渗入了他的管辖区。

sentences.en: We're renaming parts of Crown Heights as ProCro.
sentences.zh: 我们正在把皇冠高地的部分地区重新命名为普罗克罗。

sentences.en: That's ProCro.
sentences.zh: 那就是普罗克罗。

sentences.en: P-R-O-C-R-O.
sentences.zh: P-R-O-C-R-O。

sentences.en: Which is a combination, apparently, of the Prospect Heights neighborhood and Crown Heights to its eaSt.
sentences.zh: 这显然是展望高地街区与其东侧皇冠高地的结合。

sentences.en: Properties in Prospect Heights have generally sold for more than those in Crown Heights.
sentences.zh: 展望高地的房产售价通常比皇冠高地的高。

sentences.en: By making this new neighborhood, ProCro,
sentences.zh: 通过创造这个新街区普罗克罗，

sentences.en: brokers could sell Crown Heights properties at Prospect Heights prices.
sentences.zh: 经纪人就能以展望高地的价格出售皇冠高地的房产。

sentences.en: Congressman Jeffries did not like anything about this.
sentences.zh: 杰弗里斯议员对这一切都不满意。

sentences.en: He didn't like the sound of ProCro, and he didn't like what the name was trying to do.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢普罗克罗这个名字听起来的感觉，也不喜欢这个名字试图达到目的。

sentences.en: So he tried to stop it.
sentences.zh: 所以他试图阻止它。

sentences.en: When we returned out that there was no sort of governmental entity involved in the designation of neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 当我们发现没有任何政府实体参与街区的命名时。

sentences.en: In 2011, Jeffries proposed the Neighborhood Integrity Act,
sentences.zh: 2011年，杰弗里斯提出了《街区完整性法案》，

sentences.en: which set out to create guidelines and regulations for new neighborhood names and boundaries.
sentences.zh: 该法案旨在为新街区名称和边界制定准则和规章。

sentences.en: But it turned out that it's hard to pass a law against names.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，反对名字的法律很难通过。

sentences.en: The Neighborhood Integrity Act didn't gain traction.
sentences.zh: 《街区完整性法案》没有获得支持。

sentences.en: But neither did the name ProCro.
sentences.zh: 但普罗克罗这个名字也没有。

sentences.en: Well, I should point out, some names don't stick ProCro.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我得指出，有些名字流传不下来，比如普罗克罗。

sentences.en: You never really know which of these names will stick around.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道这些名字里到底哪个能流传下来。

sentences.en: Like, there's this part of Midtown Manhattan that was recently renamed Nomad for North of Madison Avenue.
sentences.zh: 就像曼哈顿中城这片区域最近被重新命名为诺玛，取自麦迪逊大道以北。

sentences.en: And people are starting to use it.
sentences.zh: 人们开始使用这个名字了。

sentences.en: You can see it on Google Maps.
sentences.zh: 你可以在谷歌地图上看到它。

sentences.en: And it's weird.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪。

sentences.en: There's not really a name for this naming convention.
sentences.zh: 这种命名惯例其实并没有一个名称。

sentences.en: Like, NOHO, SOBRO, NOMA.
sentences.zh: 比如诺霍、索布罗、诺玛。

sentences.en: They're not quite acronyMs.
sentences.zh: 它们算不上首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: They're not quite portmanteau.
sentences.zh: 它们算不上混成词。

sentences.en: They're not just abbreviations.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是缩写。

sentences.en: Around the office, we've been calling them acronyMs.
sentences.zh: 在办公室里，我们一直管它们叫首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: Or, if you want to get in the spirit of the thing, ACNAS.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你想应应景，就叫“阿克纳斯”。

sentences.en: ACNAS is too much.
sentences.zh: 阿克纳斯太过头了。

sentences.en: That's not going to be a thing.
sentences.zh: 那不会流行起来的。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They're acronyMs.
sentences.zh: 它们就是首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: And they trace their lineage back to SOHO, short for South of Houston Street in New York.
sentences.zh: 它们的渊源可以追溯到纽约的索霍，即休斯顿街以南的简称。

sentences.en: It's really interesting how SOHO developed first as a local neighborhood brand and then became globalized.
sentences.zh: 索霍最初是如何作为一个本地街区品牌发展起来，然后又走向全球化的，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Sharon Zuckin is a professor of sociology at Brooklyn College and the Graduate Center of the City University of New York.
sentences.zh: 莎朗·祖金是布鲁克林学院和纽约城市大学研究生中心的社会学教授。

sentences.en: You have neighborhoods of Boston and Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 波士顿、华盛顿特区、

sentences.en: and Seattle and Denver abbreviated as Lodo, Sodo, Soma, Sowa trading on the brand name of SOHO.
sentences.zh: 西雅图和丹佛都有街区被简称为洛多、索多、索玛、索娃，它们都借用了索霍的品牌名称。

sentences.en: Now, there already was a SOHO district in London, but as the illusionist Helen Zaltzman will tell you, that is not an acronym.
sentences.zh: 现在，伦敦已经有一个索霍区了，但正如魔术师海伦·扎尔茨曼会告诉你的一样，那不是一个首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: Most of the evidence points to it having been a hunting cry.
sentences.zh: 大部分证据表明它曾是一声狩猎呐喊。

sentences.en: SOHO!
sentences.zh: 索霍！

sentences.en: Like, Tally Ho!
sentences.zh: 就像，塔利·霍！

sentences.en: Because SOHO stands on what used to be hunting land.
sentences.zh: 因为索霍坐落在以前的狩猎土地上。

sentences.en: Other people will tell you that SOHO is a shortening of south of Hoburn, but those people are willfully ignoring the fact that SOHO is actually west of the area of Hoburn,
sentences.zh: 其他人会告诉你索霍是霍本以南的缩写，但这些人完全忽视了一个事实，即索霍实际上在霍本地区的西边，

sentences.en: which would make SOHO we-ho, which it isn't.
sentences.zh: 这会使索霍变成“韦霍”，但它并不是。

sentences.en: London's SOHO may have been first, but the American abbreviation of SOHO and the birth of the acronym can be traced back to 1962 and a fellow by the name of Chester Rapkin.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的索霍可能是最早的，但美国的索霍缩写和首字母缩略词的诞生可以追溯到1962年一个名叫切斯特·拉普金的人。

sentences.en: He was an urban planner and eventually a member of the New York City Planning Commission from the late 60s to the late 1970s,
sentences.zh: 他是一名城市规划师，后来在20世纪60年代末到70年代末担任纽约市规划委员会成员，

sentences.en: and he was asked to investigate the conditions in what he called, or what the City Planning Commission called, the South Houston Industrial Area.
sentences.zh: 他被要求调查他所谓的或城市规划委员会所谓的南休斯顿工业区的状况。

sentences.en: A lot of people think that the resulting paper, known as the Rapkin Report, invented the term SOHO.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为由此产生的被称为《拉普金报告》的文件发明了“索霍”这个词。

sentences.en: Now, I have recently re-read that report, and I do not believe that Rapkin used the term SOHO in that report.
sentences.zh: 现在，我最近重读了那份报告，我不认为拉普金在那份报告中使用了“索霍”这个词。

sentences.en: It's also been said that Rapkin coined the term SOHO in conversation, however it happened, around this time.
sentences.zh: 也有人说拉普金是在大约这个时候的对话中创造了“索霍”这个词的，不管它是怎么发生的。

sentences.en: People seized upon the term SOHO as an abbreviation.
sentences.zh: 人们抓住“索霍”这个词作为缩写。

sentences.en: Which was certainly better than the South Houston Industrial Area, but not nearly as badass as its previous name, Hell's Hundred Acres.
sentences.zh: 这当然比“南休斯顿工业区”要好，但远没有它以前的名字“地狱百英亩”那么霸气。

sentences.en: In the 1950s and early 60s, SOHO was zoned for industrial manufacturing, but a lot of the buildings were empty.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代和60年代初，索霍被划为工业制造业用地，但许多建筑都是空的。

sentences.en: At the time Rapkin was writing the report, it was not the most pleasant part of town.
sentences.zh: 在拉普金撰写报告时，这里并不是城区最宜人的地方。

sentences.en: He mentioned in passing the grim caverns of factory buildings in SOHO, and that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 他在字里行间提到了索霍工厂建筑阴森的洞穴，这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: The South Houston Industrial Area was threatened with demolition.
sentences.zh: 南休斯顿工业区面临着被拆除的威胁。

sentences.en: The brick buildings with cast-iron facades were seen as ugly, outdated eyesores.
sentences.zh: 那些带有铸铁外墙的砖砌建筑被视为丑陋、过时的眼中钉。

sentences.en: I mean, they were factories, smack in the middle of downtown Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们是工厂，就坐落在曼哈顿市中心的中央。

sentences.en: There had been a major pressure on the part of city government, as well as probably the real estate industry,
sentences.zh: 市政府以及房地产行业可能都曾施加过巨大压力，

sentences.en: to demolish these worthless buildings and replace them with one of the new residential projects.
sentences.zh: 要求拆除这些毫无价值的建筑，并用新的住宅项目取代它们。

sentences.en: This was in the early 60s, when New York City, under the influence of Robert Moses, was trying to tear down and rebuild.
sentences.zh: 这是在60年代初，当时在罗伯特·摩西的影响下，纽约市正试图大肆拆除和重建。

sentences.en: They were wrecking ball happy.
sentences.zh: 他们对拆迁球充满狂热。

sentences.en: But the Rapkin report made a plea to preserve the factory buildings, and the city held off on their plan.
sentences.zh: 但拉普金的报告呼吁保护这些工厂建筑，于是该市搁置了他们的计划。

sentences.en: Rapkin said the manufacturers in those buildings were viable, and it would be interesting, maybe even great,
sentences.zh: 拉普金表示，这些建筑里的制造商是有生存能力的，如果能把这些制造建筑翻新用于制造用途，

sentences.en: if the manufacturing buildings were renovated for manufacturing use.
sentences.zh: 那将会很有趣，甚至可能很棒。

sentences.en: Nobody foresaw that the area would become colonized by artists.
sentences.zh: 没有人预见到这个地区会被艺术家们占领。

sentences.en: Artists rented the manufacturing spaces for studios, and to save money, they lived there, too.
sentences.zh: 艺术家们租下制造空间作为工作室，为了省钱，他们也住在那里。

sentences.en: Soho, in the 1970s, quickly gained the identity of an artist district.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代的苏荷区迅速获得了艺术家聚居区的美誉。

sentences.en: But the lofts weren't supposed to be residential.
sentences.zh: 但这些阁楼本不应该是住宅。

sentences.en: They weren't up to city housing standards, state standards, fire codes, anything.
sentences.zh: 它们不符合城市的住房标准、州标准、消防规范以及任何标准。

sentences.en: For a while, the city skirted around this problem by classifying artists as machines who manufactured art
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，该市通过将艺术家归类为制造艺术品的机器来规避这个问题，

sentences.en: and could thus stay in the factories overnight.
sentences.zh: 因此他们可以在工厂过夜。

sentences.en: Performers and painters and musicians hosted happenings and art openings out of their lofts,
sentences.zh: 表演者、画家和音乐家在他们的阁楼里举办即兴活动和艺术开幕式，

sentences.en: and these attracted attention from arts publications and newspapers.
sentences.zh: 这些活动吸引了艺术出版物和报纸的关注。

sentences.en: Soho was, if not the very first industrial district to be transformed into live work and living space.
sentences.zh: 苏荷区就算不是第一个转变为居住和生活空间的工业区，

sentences.en: It was certainly the most prominent in the media.
sentences.zh: 也绝对是媒体中最引人注目的一个。

sentences.en: After the success of Soho, the urban planning department wanted to do on purpose what had happened by accident in Soho.
sentences.zh: 在苏荷区成功之后，城市规划部门希望刻意复制在苏荷区偶然发生的事情。

sentences.en: They set their sights on a nearby area, the triangle below Canal Street, or as they called it, Tribeca.
sentences.zh: 他们将目光投向了附近的一个区域，即运河街下方的三角形地带，或者正如他们所称的翠贝卡。

sentences.en: Tribeca was also a former manufacturing district, but it was intentionally rezoned for mixed use.
sentences.zh: 翠贝卡曾经也是一个工业区，但它被刻意重新规划为混合用途区。

sentences.en: So now factories and residences and galleries could exist side by side, legally.
sentences.zh: 所以现在工厂、住宅和画廊可以合法地并存。

sentences.en: You know the story from here.
sentences.zh: 你从这里开始就知道了这个故事。

sentences.en: Artists moved into the old lofts, made them seem hip and desirable,
sentences.zh: 艺术家们搬进旧阁楼，使它们看起来时髦且令人向往，

sentences.en: and higher income residences and businesses slowly took over.
sentences.zh: 更高收入的住宅和企业慢慢接管了这里。

sentences.en: And now, of course, Soho and Tribeca are fancy, fancy places, full of boutiques and high-end residences,
sentences.zh: 当然，现在苏荷和翠贝卡是高级得不得了的地方，到处都是精品店和高端住宅，

sentences.en: all housed in the architectural skeletons of old industry.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都装在老工业的建筑骨架里。

sentences.en: Soho was able to incubate and disseminate all of these trends that became so important
sentences.zh: 苏荷区能够孕育和传播所有这些在80年代和90年代室内设计中变得如此重要的趋势，

sentences.en: in interior design in the 80s and 90s, and, you know, probably on into the 2000s.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，可能一直延续到2000年代。

sentences.en: Soho and Tribeca weren't just the rise of acronyMs.
sentences.zh: 苏荷和翠贝卡不仅仅是首字母缩略词的兴起。

sentences.en: They were the birth of industrial chic.
sentences.zh: 它们是工业时尚的诞生。

sentences.en: They created the whole aesthetic that comes to mind with these neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 它们创造了人们一想到这些街区就会浮现的整体美学。

sentences.en: In Soho, artists embraced the vestiges of the factories they were living and working in.
sentences.zh: 在苏荷区，艺术家们拥抱了他们生活和工作的工厂的遗迹。

sentences.en: They found the big metal fixtures and beams and loading docks charming.
sentences.zh: 他们发现大型金属固定装置、横梁和卸货平台很有魅力。

sentences.en: And this became a kind of expensive minimalism that marked high-status taste in interior design.
sentences.zh: 这成为了一种昂贵的极简主义，标志着室内设计中的高地位审美品味。

sentences.en: Exposed brick walls, distressed floors, big windows, large open spaces, big beams and bronze fixtures.
sentences.zh: 裸露的砖墙、破旧的地板、巨大的窗户、宽敞的开放空间、大横梁和青铜固定装置。

sentences.en: The old factories became trendy.
sentences.zh: 老工厂变得时髦起来。

sentences.en: And new, wealthier residents added layers of conventional luxury.
sentences.zh: 富裕的新居民增添了传统奢华的色彩。

sentences.en: Now people install very expensive marble baths and floors and wine vaults into former industrial lofts
sentences.zh: 现在，人们在以前的工业阁楼里安装非常昂贵的大理石浴室、地板和酒窖，

sentences.en: so that the simplicity of the first generation of industrial chic
sentences.zh: 以至于第一代工业时尚的朴素，

sentences.en: has turned into the excess of the current multimillion-dollar lofts.
sentences.zh: 已经演变成如今价值数百万美元的阁楼的奢华。

sentences.en: Lofts in these genuine old buildings now go for millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 这些真正的老建筑里的阁楼现在售价高达数百万美元。

sentences.en: And new condos and developments are actively trying to look like old warehouses.
sentences.zh: 新的公寓和开发项目都在积极地试图看起来像旧仓库。

sentences.en: And in other parts of New York and other cities around the world,
sentences.zh: 在纽约的其他地方以及世界其他城市，

sentences.en: developers started to copy Soho, not just in industrial areas,
sentences.zh: 开发商开始模仿苏荷区，不仅在工业区，

sentences.en: but in all kinds of neighborhoods, independent of whoever was already living or working there.
sentences.zh: 而且在各种街区，无论当时谁已经在那里生活或工作。

sentences.en: Real estate developers around the world copy this and they say,
sentences.zh: 世界各地的房地产开发商都在模仿这一点，他们说，

sentences.en: let's bring some stores, let's encourage some performance spaces, some art galleries.
sentences.zh: 让我们带一些商店进来，鼓励一些表演空间和艺术画廊。

sentences.en: Let's make this area interesting.
sentences.zh: 让这个地区变得有趣起来。

sentences.en: Let's give it a name.
sentences.zh: 给它起个名字。

sentences.en: And as time went on, a new name, especially an acronym,
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，一个新名字，尤其是首字母缩略词，

sentences.en: became the big indicator that your neighborhood was about to change.
sentences.zh: 成为了你的街区即将发生巨变的重大指标。

sentences.en: What we're seeing is something of an era of gentrification.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所看到的是某种程度的士绅化时代。

sentences.en: This is Jacqueline Huang, a postdoctoral research fellow at Princeton University.
sentences.zh: 这是杰奎琳·黄（Jacqueline Huang），普林斯顿大学的博士后研究员。

sentences.en: In 2006, she did a comprehensive study of residents in a section of South Philadelphia,
sentences.zh: 2006年，她对南费城某个街区的居民进行了一项全面的研究，

sentences.en: where she basically went up to them and asked,
sentences.zh: 当时她基本上是走到他们面前，然后问他们：

sentences.en: what do you call your neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 你们管自己的社区叫什么名字？

sentences.en: So in this section of Philly, most of the minority residents referred to it as South Philly.
sentences.zh: 所以在费城的这个片区，大多数少数族裔居民都把它叫做南费城。

sentences.en: But not the new mostly white residents and the real estate agents
sentences.zh: 但那些新搬来的多为白人的居民、房地产经纪人却不这么叫

sentences.en: and Craigslist posts that listed the properties.
sentences.zh: 还有发布房源信息的分类广告网站也是如此。

sentences.en: Most commonly, they use the name Graduate Hospital,
sentences.zh: 他们最常用的名字是“研究生医院区”，

sentences.en: so named because a hospital used to be in that neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫这个名字，是因为以前那个街区里有一家医院。

sentences.en: Other people have referred to it as Jiho, Soso,
sentences.zh: 还有人管它叫“吉霍”或“索索”，

sentences.en: which is Soso represents south of South Street.
sentences.zh: 其中“索索”代表的是南街以南。

sentences.en: Even if they groaned or laughed at Jiho or Soso,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们对“吉霍”或“索索”这些名字感到不满或大笑，

sentences.en: these newcomers really identified more with Graduate Hospital than South Philly.
sentences.zh: 但这些新来者相比于南费城，确实对“研究生医院区”更有认同感。

sentences.en: Now, just to be clear, neighborhoods do shift and change names periodically.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，需要说明的是，社区确实会定期更名和发生变化。

sentences.en: But Jacqueline says the recent naming rush is different.
sentences.zh: 但杰奎琳说，最近这股起名热潮有所不同。

sentences.en: I would say that there's an intention behind this and sort of a power play happening.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，这背后是有意图的，可以说是一场权力较量。

sentences.en: You know, there's a group that's redefining it,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有一个群体在试图重新定义它，

sentences.en: while another group is trying to hold on to this older name.
sentences.zh: 而另一个群体则在努力守住这个更古老的名称。

sentences.en: As cities boom and gentrification rises,
sentences.zh: 随着城市蓬勃发展和士绅化现象加剧，

sentences.en: new neighborhoods get made and new names proliferate.
sentences.zh: 新的社区不断涌现，新的名字也层出不穷。

sentences.en: I'm not saying neighborhood change is not good for these neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说社区的变化对这些社区没有好处。

sentences.en: They certainly need the investment,
sentences.zh: 它们确实需要投资，

sentences.en: but I think the idea that there's this alienation that's taking place
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种正在发生的疏离感，

sentences.en: and that, you know, it's intentional of displacing and devaluing the previous name
sentences.zh: 你知道的，是有意在取代和贬低原有的名字，

sentences.en: in order to make the neighborhood change faster.
sentences.zh: 以此来加快社区变化的步伐。

sentences.en: This gets at the ickiness I feel about using the term noby to describe where I live.
sentences.zh: 这就触及了我对用“诺比”这个词来形容我住的地方时所感到的那种别扭。

sentences.en: I don't want to be the newcomer who alienates the old residents
sentences.zh: 我不想成为那个让老居民感到疏离的新来者，

sentences.en: by using some term that was fed to me by real estate developers.
sentences.zh: 去使用房地产开发商塞给我的某个词。

sentences.en: But noby is also useful because it's specific and it's efficient.
sentences.zh: 但“诺比”也有它的用处，因为它具体而且高效。

sentences.en: I mean, saying I live in noby is obviously faster than saying
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说我住在“诺比”显然比说

sentences.en: I live at the border of North Oakland, Berkeley, and Emeryville.
sentences.zh: 我住在北奥克兰、伯克利和埃默里维尔的交界处要快得多。

sentences.en: Well, I live in Dobie, which is downtown Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我住在“多比”，也就是伯克利市中心。

sentences.en: I just made up the name Dobie.
sentences.zh: “多比”这个名字是我刚编出来的。

sentences.en: That is comedian and longtime Bay Area resident W.
sentences.zh: 那位是喜剧演员兼湾区老居民W·

sentences.en: Kamau Bell.
sentences.zh: 卡马乌·贝尔（W. Kamau Bell）。

sentences.en: I was thinking about my neighborhood and gentrification
sentences.zh: 我当时正在思考我的社区和士绅化的问题，

sentences.en: when I happened to run into him, appropriately,
sentences.zh: 恰好遇到了他，说来也巧，

sentences.en: at the South Berkeley Farmer's Market.
sentences.zh: 地点就在南伯克利农夫市场。

sentences.en: I know they call it the South Berkeley Farmer's Market,
sentences.zh: 我知道他们管这叫南伯克利农夫市场，

sentences.en: but I've lived in the Bay Area long enough to remember
sentences.zh: 但我住在湾区的时间够久，还记得

sentences.en: when this was called Oakland right here.
sentences.zh: 这里以前被称为奥克兰的时候。

sentences.en: This feels like South, South, South, South, South, Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 这里感觉像是南、南、南、南、南伯克利。

sentences.en: Kamau feels uncomfortable with these acronyms, too.
sentences.zh: 卡马乌对这些缩写词也感到不舒服。

sentences.en: Kono, which they're trying to make downtown.
sentences.zh: 比如“科诺”，他们正试图把它打造成市中心。

sentences.en: Oh, no, what is that?
sentences.zh: 哦不，那是什么？

sentences.en: Koreatown Northgate.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜城北门区（Koreatown Northgate）。

sentences.en: Kono?
sentences.zh: 科诺？

sentences.en: Kono.
sentences.zh: 科诺。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不要啊。

sentences.en: But he says if you're focused too much on neighborhood names,
sentences.zh: 但他说，如果你把太多注意力放在社区名字上，

sentences.en: you might be missing the point.
sentences.zh: 你可能就抓不住重点了。

sentences.en: This is just symptomatic of like,
sentences.zh: 这只是一种症状，就像是，

sentences.en: this is like, the neighborhood name is like the old log in the woods,
sentences.zh: 社区的名字就像是树林里的一截老原木，

sentences.en: and you lift up the neighborhood name and you see all the bugs underneath,
sentences.zh: 你掀开社区名字这截原木，就会看到底下所有的虫子，

sentences.en: and that's gentrification.
sentences.zh: 而那就是士绅化。

sentences.en: If you get too focused on the name,
sentences.zh: 如果你过分关注名字，

sentences.en: you're probably not focused on what's going on under the wood.
sentences.zh: 你可能就不会去关注木头底下到底在发生什么。

sentences.en: Acronyms are easy to lampoon.
sentences.zh: 缩写词很容易成为嘲讽的对象。

sentences.en: They're ubiquitous to the point of parody and often cringeworthy.
sentences.zh: 它们无处不在，甚至达到了荒谬的地步，而且常常让人觉得尴尬。

sentences.en: So we may see a shift away from these names.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会看到人们开始摒弃这些名字。

sentences.en: Real estate developers will start using less silly-sounding names to market neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 房地产开发商将开始使用听起来不那么傻的名字来向

sentences.en: to higher-paying customers.
sentences.zh: 支付能力更强的客户营销社区。

sentences.en: These names might sound more authentic, like Graduate Hospital in Philly or Temescal in Oakland,
sentences.zh: 这些名字听起来可能更地道，比如费城的“研究生医院区”或奥克兰的“特梅斯卡尔”，

sentences.en: but they're different names for the same thing,
sentences.zh: 但它们只是换汤不换药的同一个东西，

sentences.en: the same log over the ants of gentrification.
sentences.zh: 也就是压在士绅化这群蚂蚁之上的同一截原木。

sentences.en: And as far as what you should call your neighborhood, if you're a newcomer?
sentences.zh: 至于如果你是一个新来者，你应该怎么称呼你的社区？

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like the bigger issue is to respect the neighborhood you're moving into.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得更重要的问题是要尊重你搬进去的那个社区。

sentences.en: If you respect the neighborhood you're moving into,
sentences.zh: 如果你尊重你搬进去的社区，

sentences.en: and you aren't trying to be the change, you're trying to be the blend,
sentences.zh: 而且你不是想成为那个带来改变的人，而是想融入其中，

sentences.en: then you should, then whatever the people in the neighborhood call it,
sentences.zh: 那么你就应该，社区里的人怎么叫它，

sentences.en: then call it that.
sentences.zh: 你就怎么叫它。

sentences.en: So I took Kamau's advice.
sentences.zh: 所以我采纳了卡马乌的建议。

sentences.en: I walked around my block, and I asked people,
sentences.zh: 我在我的街区四周走了走，问了问大家：

sentences.en: what do you call this neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 你们管这个社区叫什么？

sentences.en: And I met a few newcomers, like me, who were just as confused as I was.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了一些像我一样的新来者，他们和我一样迷茫。

sentences.en: Was it Noby?
sentences.zh: 是叫“诺比”吗？

sentences.en: Was it the Ashby-Bart region?
sentences.zh: 是阿什比-巴特（Ashby-Bart）地区吗？

sentences.en: The Golden Gate District?
sentences.zh: 金门区？

sentences.en: The Loren District?
sentences.zh: 洛伦区？

sentences.en: But the neighbors who've lived here for a while all said the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但那些在这里住了一段时间的邻居们都异口同声地说：

sentences.en: It's just North Oakland.
sentences.zh: 这就是北奥克兰。

sentences.en: And really, it doesn't need to be called anything else.
sentences.zh: 真的，它根本不需要被叫成别的什么名字。

sentences.en: Can I put you on 99%?
sentences.zh: 能把我放进《99%无形》节目里吗？

sentences.en: Can I use this tape?
sentences.zh: 我能用这盘磁带吗？

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: Can you put me on 99% Invisible?
sentences.zh: 你能把我弄进《99%无形》吗？

sentences.en: Hashtag life goals.
sentences.zh: 人生目标大加号。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Avery Truffleman,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》由埃弗里·特拉夫曼（Avery Truffleman）制作，

sentences.en: with Katie Mingle, Sam Greenspan, Delaney Hall,
sentences.zh: 合作制片人包括凯蒂·明格（Katie Mingle）、萨姆·格林斯潘（Sam Greenspan）、德兰妮·霍尔（Delaney Hall）、

sentences.en: Kirk Kohlstedt, Sharif Youssef, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 柯克·科尔施泰特（Kirk Kohlstedt）、谢里夫·尤塞夫（Sharif Youssef），还有我，罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Jeff Bliss, Tim Wong, W.
sentences.zh: 本周要特别感谢杰夫·布利斯（Jeff Bliss）、蒂姆·黄（Tim Wong）、W·

sentences.en: Kamau Bell, and Helen Zaltzman.
sentences.zh: 卡马乌·贝尔和海伦·扎尔特曼（Helen Zaltzman）。

sentences.en: You should already be downloading Helen's Radiotopia podcast,
sentences.zh: 你们应该已经在自己喜爱的播客应用上下载海伦的电台乌托邦（Radiotopia）播客了，

sentences.en: The Illusionist, on your favorite podcasting app.
sentences.zh: 也就是《幻觉师》（The Illusionist）。

sentences.en: But if not, take this opportunity to remedy that.
sentences.zh: 如果还没有，请趁这个机会补上。

sentences.en: Kamau Bell hosts a new radio show and podcast called Kamau Right Now,
sentences.zh: 卡马乌·贝尔主持了一档名为《卡马乌现在就来》（Kamau Right Now）的新广播节目和播客，

sentences.en: which I highly recommend.
sentences.zh: 我强烈推荐。

sentences.en: It's a live talk show based here in the Bay.
sentences.zh: 这是一档立足于湾区的现场脱口秀节目。

sentences.en: It's produced by KALW, the greatest radio station in the world.
sentences.zh: 它由世界上最伟大的广播电台KALW制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州美丽市中心奥克兰的

sentences.en: an architecture and interiors firm, in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 建筑与室内设计公司 ArcSign 的办公室里制作完成。

sentences.en: You can find the show and join the fine community of people who like this show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书上找到这个节目，并加入喜欢这个节目的优秀粉丝群体。

sentences.en: I fave every 99PI coin I see on Twitter and Instagram.
sentences.zh: 我在推特和照片墙上看到每一个 99PI 的硬币我都会点赞。

sentences.en: Every single one of them makes me happy when I see them.
sentences.zh: 只要看到它们，每一个都会让我感到开心。

sentences.en: So please keep sending them in.
sentences.zh: 所以请继续把它们发给我们吧。

sentences.en: But if you want to explore the 99% invisible activity that shapes the design of our world,
sentences.zh: 但如果你想探索塑造我们世界设计的《99%无形》活动，

sentences.en: I recommend you spend some time perusing 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 我建议你花点时间浏览 99PI.org。

sentences.zh: 电台乌托邦。
